bulk_download_formats.description: Available formats for bulk data download, such as CSV or GeoJSON, if any.

data_management_body.description: The specific department responsible for the data, e.g., 'DRPT for transit and rail projects'.

is_technically_feasible.description: An assessment of whether joining VDOT and Richmond CIP data is possible.

common_project_identifier.description: The shared data field that could be used to join the datasets, such as 'UPC' (Universal Project Code).

identified_challenges.description: Potential obstacles to successful data integration, such as data consistency or differing update schedules.

city_name.description: The name of the mid-size U.S. city with a successful dashboard.

dashboard_status.description: The current operational status of the dashboard, e.g., 'Active and regularly updated'.

key_governance_factors.description: The governance structures or practices that contribute to the dashboard's success, such as a dedicated PMO or clear update cadence.

successful_municipal_dashboards.description: Case studies of mid-size U.S. cities that have successfully maintained a capital projects dashboard with regular updates for more than two years. Will be detailed in step 2 to include city name, dashboard status, and key governance factors.

governance_models_for_successful_dashboa.description: Analysis of the governance structures, such as dedicated Project Management Offices (PMOs) or inter-departmental working groups, that contributed to the longevity and success of the identified municipal dashboards.

report_source.description: The official source of the analysis, e.g., 'NYC Comptroller's Office report Flying Blind on Billions'.

project_id_coverage_percentage.description: The percentage of Financial Management System (FMS) IDs included in the dashboard.

last_known_status.description: The state of the dashboard at the time of the report, e.g., '6 months without an update'.

identified_weaknesses.description: A summary of the key problems identified, such as data incompleteness, inconsistent identifiers, and lack of timeliness.

lessons_for_richmond_from_nyc.description: Key lessons and strategic recommendations for Richmond based on the challenges faced by NYC's dashboard, focusing on data completeness, standardized identifiers, and robust governance.

static_geojson_architecture_evaluation.description: An evaluation of the proposal for Richmond to adopt a nightly ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) to a static GeoJSON architecture. This analysis covers the potential benefits for decoupling resident-facing tools from upstream data source changes and improving reliability.

dashboard_name.description: The official name of Richmond's dashboard.

current_status.description: The developmental stage of the dashboard, e.g., 'Beta Version'.

technology_platform.description: The underlying software used to build the dashboard, e.g., 'ArcGIS Experience Builder'.

stated_update_frequency.description: The frequency at which the city claims to update the dashboard data, e.g., 'Quarterly'.

governing_document_name.description: The official name of the manual or standard that governs work area safety, e.g., 'Virginia Work Area Protection Manual (WAPM)'.

issuing_authority.description: The organization that publishes and maintains the standard, e.g., 'VDOT'.

relevance.description: How the document applies to the query, e.g., 'Provides guidelines for safe and ADA-compliant pedestrian detours in construction zones'.
